extracted.intended_audience: funding agency staff, grant program designers, researchers of peer review and gender bias
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating grant review rubrics for funding competitions, with attention to whether criteria emphasize the proposed science or the principal investigator, and how that affects gender gaps in funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate primarily the quality of the proposed research (explicit criterion in the science-focused 'Project Grant' program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes emphasis on scientific merit independent of applicant identity. The study finds that rubrics focusing reviewers on the proposed work (rather than the PI) reduce gender disparities; thus weight this criterion to center evaluation on the science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of the research question
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how important or consequential the proposed research question is (explicit criterion in the 'Project Grant' program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the science-focused evaluation dimensions; prioritizing significance over investigator attributes is associated with smaller gender gaps in funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the proposed study's methods, including rigor, appropriateness, and experimental or analytic design (explicit 'Project Grant' criterion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize methodological rigor as a core, objective basis for scoring; focusing reviewer attention on methods helps shift judgment away from applicant characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the proposed research is likely to be achievable with the outlined approach and resources (explicit 'Project Grant' criterion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use feasibility as a concrete, project-based criterion to anchor reviewer evaluations in tangible aspects of the proposal rather than PI reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibre / track record of the principal investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the PI's overall calibre, including past accomplishments and perceived competence (primary focus in the 'Foundation Grant' program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study demonstrates that emphasizing PI calibre amplifies gender bias: female applicants received significantly less favourable assessments under PI-focused review (gap widened to ~4.0 percentage points). Use caution when weighting or privileging this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research direction / vision
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the principal investigator's research direction and long-term vision (explicit 'Foundation Grant' criterion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a PI-focused, often more subjective dimension; the paper's findings suggest subjective PI-focused criteria can widen gender disparities in funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the PI's past productivity (publications, outputs) and their impact (citations, influence) (explicit 'Foundation Grant' criterion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures of productivity/impact are commonly used to assess PI calibre but may be vulnerable to bias; consider how raw productivity metrics and their interpretation could differentially disadvantage women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects of the proposed program
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of particular features of the proposed program of research (included among Foundation Grant criteria along with PI assessment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in PI-focused programs some program-level elements are judged; however, when PI criteria dominate, these elements may receive less weight, with implications for fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighting between investigator-focused and science-focused criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: How much score weight (explicit or implicit) the rubric assigns to investigator/track-record criteria versus project/science criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key design variable: the study's natural experiment shows that higher weight on investigator criteria amplifies gender gaps, whereas emphasizing science criteria reduces them. Recommendation: shift weight away from investigator metrics toward project-based metrics to mitigate gender bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization / redaction of applicant identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural design choice to remove or redact PI-identifying information from applications or reviews to reduce bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommend trials of redaction/anonymization as a practical measure to reduce gender disparities by preventing evaluators from focusing on PI identity or track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of natural-experiment or other designs to isolate rubric effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological standard: exploit programmatic changes or comparable conditions to isolate the causal effect of rubric focus on outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses CIHR's 2014 split into Project vs Foundation programs (same applicants, same agency, same time) to isolate rubric focus effects. Similar designs help separate rubric-driven bias from confounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment for applicant age and research domain in outcome analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytic practice to control for applicant age and research domain when estimating gender gaps in funding success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study adjusted for these covariates; such adjustments are important to distinguish rubric-induced disparities from composition differences across applicant groups.
